record.original_question: A set B N is called a basis of order 2 if any positive integer is representable as a sum of two elements of B. Does there exist a basis B of order 2 such that the number-of-representations function B(n) := jf(b1; b2) 2 B B : b1 + b2 = ngj is uniformly bounded by a constant, independent on n? Erd}os conjectured that the answer is negative. We refer the reader to for exciting partial results towards the solution of this problem and its nite analogues.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ a basis of order $2$ if every sufficiently large positive integer can be written as $b_1 + b_2$ with $b_1, b_2 \in B$. For such a set define the representation function
$$r_B(n) := \#\{(b_1, b_2) \in B \times B : b_1 + b_2 = n\}.$$
Does there exist a basis $B$ of order $2$ for which $r_B$ is uniformly bounded, i.e., there is a constant $C$ with $r_B(n) \le C$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$? (Equivalently, prove or disprove that for every basis $B$ of order $2$, $\limsup_{n\to\infty} r_B(n) = \infty$.)
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases (1941). It remains open. Partial results establish that for any asymptotic basis of order 2 the representation function must exceed certain explicit constants infinitely often (e.g., ≥ 6 by Grekos et al. 2003, improved to ≥ 8 by Borwein–Choi–Chu), but no proof of unboundedness is known.
